artworks.title: The Residence (1901) by Henry Bacon
artworks.description: The three-floor stucco house, with nine bedrooms, mixes English Georgian, American Colonial Revival and Italian villa ideas; it sits on a ridge with views from its porches. French’s sister-in-law Alice Helm French painted the fresco garlands on the Breakfast Porch and retouched them for 31 years. The rooms keep family heirlooms and antiques French bought at local auctions; doors and moldings came from the old Warner farmhouse. Seen on the guided tour.

artworks.imageCredit: Daderot, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: The piazza

artworks.title: The Casting Room

artworks.title: The Studio’s Main Room
artworks.description: The main work space is a 30 by 29-foot room with 26-foot walls, high enough for heroic equestrian models. Part of the floor is a standard-gauge railroad flatcar: French removed the floor panels next to it and pushed his work outdoors on tracks to judge it in daylight, often standing down in the field to see it at the right distance. The Seated Lincoln plaster model and the marble Andromeda are here.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages
artworks.imageCredit: Daderot, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: The Studio (1898) by Henry Bacon
artworks.description: French asked his friend Henry Bacon, later the architect of the Lincoln Memorial, to design the Studio in 1897, where the old barn stood, for its view of Monument Mountain. French moved in on July 16, 1898, before it was finished. It was restored in 2014 to look as it did in French’s time.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages
artworks.imageCredit: Daderot, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: The railroad track
artworks.description: The tracks that carried French’s models out of the Studio on a flatcar, into the open air.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages
artworks.imageCredit: BakedintheHole, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: Andromeda
artworks.description: French’s last work, left unfinished when he died in October 1931. Unlike the frantic Andromedas of Rembrandt or Titian, his chained princess seems to doze in the sun; a young Stockbridge woman, Ethel Cummings, posed for her. It was the piece the Studio’s flatcar was built for. Using a Greek myth as the basis for the subject of Andromeda, French also incorporated his own belief that “the beauty of woman is beauty at its best and highest.” French’s final work, Andromeda remained incomplete at his death in October, 1931.

artworks.title: Spirit of Life (Spencer Trask Memorial)
artworks.description: Bronze statue in Congress Park, Saratoga Springs, NY. Spencer Trask (1844–1909) was a prominent business man and his home, Yaddo, is now an artist’s retreat. The Memorial was commissioned by his wife, Katrina Trask, and close friend George Foster Peabody, to commemorate Trask’s life and work for the Saratoga Springs Reservation Commission.

artworks.title: Immortal Love
artworks.description: Marble sculpture at Corcoran Gallery, now under the care of the National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC. Also known as The Sons of God Saw the Daughters of Man That They Were Fair, referring to the divine sons of Gods captivated by the human daughters of men, in Genesis. The composition of the work was inspired by a photograph of an erupting geyser in Yellowstone (reproduction in photograph stand).

artworks.title: The Reception Room
artworks.description: Fashionable artists’ studios of French’s time had a reception room to receive business visitors. French also drew and painted portraits of friends, family and neighbors here in the north light, and the family took afternoon tea here when it rained. A recess in the east wall, the “Cozy Corner”, has a built-in bookcase and a Pompeian-style day bed French built for his early studio in Concord.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages

artworks.title: Fireplace & Mantel
artworks.description: Fireplace mantel shelf features egg and dart molding, a cartouche with fleur-de-lis relief, and a center frieze cast after a reproduction of a Donatello relief in Lucca, Italy. See bas-relief below.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s Guide to the Studio
artworks.placeNote: Reception Room (no. 1). Pieces are sometimes moved.

artworks.title: La Jeunesse
artworks.description: Polychrome glazed terra cotta sculpture of a young female in the Renaissance Revival style, by Herbert Adams. In 1899, Adams authorized a Mr. Hall to reproduce La Jeunesse in terra cotta. Adams recalls four or five copies being made, but he did not like them very much. After giving one to French, he had the others destroyed. (see American Sculpture in The Metropolitan Museum of Art: A Catalogue of Works by Artists Born Before 1865, p. 364).
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s Guide to the Studio
artworks.placeNote: Reception Room (no. 2). Pieces are sometimes moved.

artworks.title: The Studio Garden and fountain
artworks.description: French designed this formal garden in 1898 on an old apple orchard, as a series of outdoor rooms for parties, costume balls and tableaux vivants. In the round court in front of the Studio is a marble-cement fountain by Henry Bacon with dancing putti. The Straight Path, lined with standard hydrangeas and peonies, leads to the Woodland Walk; south of the Studio a pergola with benches designed by French looks out on the Berkshire Hills.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages

artworks.title: The hydrangea walk
artworks.description: The Straight Path (allée) from the fountain, lined with standard hydrangeas, peonies and annuals.
artworks.descriptionKind: From Chesterwood’s pages

artworks.title: The Woodland Walk
artworks.description: French laid out these trails around 1898 as a “classroom of nature” for his daughter Margaret: the Circle, the Glade and the Overlook, joined by footpaths with “vistas” cut through the trees. The Overlook looks across to Stockbridge, Lenox and Lee. The restored Ledges Trail climbs steeply over rocky ledges to a view at about 1,200 feet. The Woodland Walk is a mostly flat dirt path.
